title: Suvendu Adhikari Becomes Bengal's First BJP Chief Minister
excerpt: The BJP veteran took oath at Kolkata's Brigade Parade Ground on May 9, ending 15 years of Trinamool Congress rule in West Bengal.
body:
Suvendu Adhikari made history on May 9, 2026, when he was sworn in as West Bengal's ninth Chief Minister — and the first ever from the Bharatiya Janata Party — at a packed ceremony at Kolkata's Brigade Parade Ground. The oath ended a 15-year Trinamool Congress reign that once seemed unshakeable.

**What happened at Brigade Parade Ground:**
Adhikari took the oath of office at Kolkata's Brigade Parade Grounds, where Governor RN Ravi administered the oath of office and secrecy to Adhikari and five cabinet ministers in a ceremony attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and a large contingent of NDA leaders. With this oath-taking, Adhikari became Bengal's ninth Chief Minister and the first leader in 55 years from a district background, rather than Kolkata, to head the state administration.

**How the BJP got here:**
The BJP won 207 of 294 Assembly seats to end the Trinamool Congress' 15-year administration. Adhikari registered a significant personal victory by winning from Nandigram and defeating former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur. This electoral outcome brings an end to decades of non-BJP rule in the state, following nearly 34 years of Left Front governance and 15 years under the Trinamool Congress. The BJP's 'Sonar Bangla' vision — a prosperous, well-governed Bengal — drove its campaign messaging from the outset.

**What to watch next:**
Portfolios are yet to be assigned, and the new government faces the immediate task of addressing post-poll administrative challenges as it begins its inaugural term. Outgoing Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has refused to concede defeat, alleging electoral irregularities, which means the political temperature in Kolkata is unlikely to cool quickly.
